class.name: PhysXBlastAuthoring
class.brief_description: Script-callable Blast fracture authoring: turns a [Mesh] into a [PhysXBlastAsset] at runtime or in headless tool scripts.
class.description: Runs the same NVIDIA Blast authoring pipeline as the editor's in-viewport fracture dialog (the one behind right-clicking a [MeshInstance3D] in the Scene tree or a [Mesh] in the FileSystem dock), but callable from any script -- useful for batch asset generation, CI-authored test assets, or in-game procedural destruction authoring. Needs the module built with [code]blast_sdk=[/code]. The result carries the cooked NvBlast asset plus the per-chunk render geometry; feed it to a [PhysXDestructible3D] via its [member PhysXDestructible3D.blast_asset] property.

method.name: fracture_mesh
method.description: Fractures [param mesh] and returns the finished [PhysXBlastAsset], or a null reference on failure (null mesh, a mesh whose triangles don't form a closed watertight surface after the automatic cleanup pass, or [constant PATTERN_CUTOUT] without a usable [param cutout_pattern]). [param site_count] is the cell/slice count: for [constant PATTERN_VORONOI] it is the number of random cells the mesh is split into; for [constant PATTERN_SLICING] it is cut into roughly that many brick-like pieces on the longest axis; it is ignored for [constant PATTERN_CUTOUT] (the pattern texture alone defines the pieces). [param seed] makes [constant PATTERN_VORONOI] reproducible -- the same mesh, count and seed always produce the same asset. Note the mesh is authored as-is: a source [MeshInstance3D]'s node transform (including scale) is not baked in.

constants.constant: Random Voronoi cells -- organic, rock-like chunks. The default.
Evenly spaced cutting planes per axis -- regular, brick-like pieces. Good for crates and walls.

Extrudes a caller-supplied grayscale [param cutout_pattern] texture through the mesh -- glass/tile-style breaks. The cracks must reach the texture's edge (like a real broken pane) or the fracture is rejected.
